propertyRationales.cleansingStrength: SLES is the lead surfactant with Coco-Betaine support, giving strong ordinary cleansing potential.
propertyRationales.conditioningLevel: Cationic guar plus a cationic lemon protein derivative and a small emollient signal support moderate non-silicone conditioning.
propertyRationales.weightPotential: The substantive cationic polymer route and protein-film signal create moderate deposition potential, but there is no silicone or rich lipid system.
propertyRationales.focusPrimary: Although the formula has scalp-exposure and conditioning signals, blind formula alone does not establish a dominant claim-compatible role, so general is retained.
propertyRationales.focusSecondary: Secondary focus defaults to empty because no distinct product-positioning signal is available in the blind pass.
propertyRationales.usageRole: Salicylic Acid does not by itself trigger treatment use, and there is no recognized anti-dandruff active or reset positioning, so regular applies.
propertyRationales.scalpComfortTarget: Salicylic Acid, fragrance allergens and citrus components create scalp exposure flags, but the formula does not prove a scalp-comfort target and is not suitable to classify as sensitive-scalp supportive.
propertyRationales.dandruffSupport: The complete formula does not list Piroctone Olamine or Climbazole.

formulaObservations: Sodium Laureth Sulfate and Coco-Betaine form the main cleansing system.
Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride is a cationic deposition polymer.
Hydroxypropyltrimonium Lemon Protein is a cationic protein-derived film signal.
Salicylic Acid, Fumaric Acid and Citric Acid are present, but finished pH and contact-time intent are unknown.
Multiple fragrance allergens, citrus extracts and grapefruit peel oil are listed.
counterSignals: Glycol Distearate should not be treated as hair shine evidence by itself.
Salicylic Acid is not Piroctone Olamine or Climbazole and does not make dandruffSupport supported.
Carbomer may be a rheology polymer rather than a hair-depositing film.
Botanical extracts, niacinamide and vitamins do not establish a dominant scalp-active or repair focus without claims or product evidence.

finalDelta.reason: The product name and manufacturer claims emphasize Kraft/strength; formula support is compatible only as temporary cosmetic repair/surface reinforcement.
Glanz is explicit in the name/claims and has an independent smoothing/film route, so one secondary `shine` is justified; volume is left out to respect ordinary max-one secondary.

focusPrimary.formulaRoute: Cationic guar plus cationic lemon protein derivative supports temporary cosmetic strength/repair surface care.
focusPrimary.decisionReason: Kraft/kräftigendes wording is dominant; shine remains a distinct secondary because it is explicit and formula-routed.

independentFormulaRoutes: Cationic guar/protein film plus Glycol Distearate/Octyldodecanol support smoothing/reflection shine separately from the strength claim.

usageRole.rationale: No non-default trigger: strong cleansing blocks frequent, and there is no reset or recognized anti-dandruff active route.

formulaRoutes.evidence: Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride is a substantive cationic deposition route.
Hydroxypropyltrimonium Lemon Protein supports a weak-to-moderate temporary film cue.
Octyldodecanol and Glycol Distearate provide limited emollient/pearlizer support, not a rich lipid route.

competingSignals: No silicone or second substantive deposition route.
